fields.h1: Build a Stakeholder Survey That Compares Every Group
fields.hero_description: Build a stakeholder survey that tags each answer with its group and saves every response to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Stakeholder Survey Built With Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the stakeholder survey and the answer table behind it, and every answer keeps the group it came from.
fields.feature_1:
A section of questions per group

Name your groups and what you need to learn from each, and Emergent drafts a section for every one. A follow-up prompt rewrites a question or adds a group you left out.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer tagged with its group

Each response saves as a row in a database you own, with the group, the date, and the survey round attached. Put this year's donor scores beside last year's in one table.
fields.feature_3:
One link, a separate path for each role

Open with one question on who is answering, and each role then gets its own set of questions. Shared questions keep identical wording in every version, and their scores line up.
fields.feature_4:
Low group scores go to the group owner

Set a floor for any group, like an average under 3 out of 5, and the app sends that group's scores to its owner by email or Slack. Groups above the floor stay in the report.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen, no response cap

Stakeholders tap through one question per screen on a phone or a laptop. Emergent sets no cap on responses, whether the list is 12 funders or 4,000 residents of a town.
fields.feature_6:
A survey address on your own domain

Funders open the survey at an address on your own domain, since custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Acts on Each Stakeholder Survey
fields.tab_content_1:
For donors, reach comes first; for pantries, delivery days

For its 3-year plan, Harbor Lane Food Bank surveyed 4 groups and got 214 answers: 87 from volunteers, 61 from donors, 38 from partner pantries, and 28 from staff. Donors put reaching more families first; pantries chose a second weekly delivery day. Executive director Oriel Tash saw each group's top pick side by side.
fields.tab_content_2:
Receiving drops to 2.4, and the project lead sees it first

Five teams at Brightwater Supply rate monthly, on a 1 to 5 scale, how informed they feel about the new warehouse system. In August, Receiving averaged 2.4 from 17 answers, under the 3.0 floor, and every other team scored 3.6 or higher. The app emailed that team's scores and comments to the project lead, Dagny Ruel.
fields.tab_content_3:
A resident and a business owner see different questions

One link went out for Pell River's Main Street redesign, and the first question sorts people by role. Of 412 answers, 268 came from residents, 93 from commuters, and 51 from business owners. Hollis Brandt, the town planner, got a separate table: 34 of those 51 owners named loading zones as their top concern.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three partners asked for a call, all on one list

Every June, the Corvane Institute surveys its 42 industry partners on the research they fund and how well the institute reports back. This year 31 answered, and 3 ticked the box asking for a call. Those 3 went on one list for Ines Varga, the partnerships lead, each with the partner's rating and comment.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Stakeholder Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a stakeholder survey that every group finishes and that shows where the groups disagree.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the decision the answers feed
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name each group and its owner
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Split any question that asks two things
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the results will change before you write a question, such as a 3-year plan or a rollout date. A question that changes neither costs a stakeholder time and tells you nothing new. Put that decision at the top of your prompt to Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down every group you will survey, like donors and partner agencies, and the person who acts on each group's answers. Make the first question ask which group the person belongs to. Every answer then carries its group from the start.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Turn "How clear and timely are our updates?" into two questions. Pew Research Center says double-barreled questions are difficult for respondents to answer and hard to interpret. Two questions also tell you whether to fix the clarity or the timing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give every group the same core ratings, worded identically, then add a short set for each group. Identical wording is what lets you put donor scores beside staff scores. Place the ratings before the open comments, since question order can influence how people respond.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to two people from different groups and note where either one stalls or reads a question two ways. Pew calls pretesting an essential step in the questionnaire design process. Fix those questions before the full send.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link with a closing date and one reminder 3 days before it. Track answers by group as they arrive: if partner agencies sit at 6 of 40 while staff are at 30 of 35, chase the agencies, not everyone.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Show each group its own results
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month of closing, send each group its scores next to the overall result, plus the 2 changes you picked. Ask the same core questions next round, and the scores show whether those changes moved anything for that group.

faq_plan.a: A stakeholder survey is a questionnaire sent to the groups with a stake in an organization or project, such as funders, partners, staff, and neighbors, to learn what each group needs. The Project Management Institute defines a project stakeholder as an individual, group, or organization who may affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a stakeholder survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe your stakeholder groups, the questions each one should answer, and who should see each group's results, and Emergent's AI survey builder drafts the survey and the database behind it. Change any question with a follow-up prompt, then send one link to every group. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing the survey.

faq_plan.q: What stakeholder survey questions should I ask each group?
faq_plan.a: Ask every group the same 4 or 5 core ratings, such as how informed they feel and how much they trust the plan, then add a few questions only that group can answer. A partner agency might rate delivery timing, and a donor how gifts are reported. Close with one open-ended question, where people answer in their own words, on what should change.

faq_plan.q: What should a stakeholder survey template include?
faq_plan.a: A stakeholder survey template needs a role question first, a core block every group answers, a short block for each group, and one open question at the end. Use rating scales for opinions. Save yes or no items for facts, like whether someone attended the last briefing, and a yes no questions survey handles those quick checks.

faq_plan.q: What are some stakeholder survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Here are four stakeholder survey examples. A food bank asks donors, partner pantries, volunteers, and staff what its next plan should put first. A project team checks monthly how informed each department feels. A town gathers input on a street redesign, and a research institute asks industry partners how well it reports back.

faq_plan.q: Should a stakeholder survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Only if you will never need to follow up on a comment. In an anonymous survey, responses are completely separate from any personally identifiable information, and no one can call a partner back. In a confidential one, responses are connected to personal information. An app Emergent builds can store the group with each answer and leave the name out.

faq_plan.q: How long should a stakeholder survey be?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to 15 questions or fewer for groups who owe you nothing, such as partners and neighbors; staff can take a few more. Put the core ratings first and the group questions after them. Leave out warm-ups and funny survey questions, which suit a team social better than a survey that feeds a decision.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more people to answer a stakeholder survey?
faq_plan.a: Send it from the person each group already knows, say in one line which decision it feeds, and set a closing date with one reminder before it. Keep it short enough to finish on a phone. Emergent can build it as a conversational survey with one question per screen, and there are no response caps.

faq_plan.q: How do I compare stakeholder survey results across groups?
faq_plan.a: Compare each group's average on the shared questions, never one overall score, since a large group can drown out a small one. Show the answer count beside each average: a score from 6 partners is weaker evidence than one from 60 volunteers. The app Emergent builds stores every answer with its group in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Is a stakeholder survey different from a poll?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in what it is for. Use poll questions when one or two quick answers and a tally are enough, such as a fast read in a meeting. Use a stakeholder survey when each group answers a set of questions and you need to compare the groups before a plan or a budget is set.

plan.angle: Stakeholder survey searches land on question lists and templates that treat every respondent the same. A stakeholder survey earns its keep when it shows how groups differ: donors against partner agencies, one project team against the rest, residents against shop owners. This page shows four surveys built from a prompt where every answer carries its group, and each ends with a named person acting on one group's result. The FAQ covers what a builder asks: which questions, what a template needs, examples, anonymity, length, response rates, and reporting results back.
